_about: Yard shapes for the 3D view. Units are FEET. Two distances are measured (deck to shed ≈ 27.5 ft; left fence ≈ 63 ft 8 in). Everything else is estimated from photos. x runs left(-) to right(+) as seen from the deck. z is the distance out from the deck edge toward the back treeline. Change any number here to move or resize something.

site.usdaZoneSource: 2023 USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map (the newest; built from 1991–2020 data), looked up for Salem, MA via phzmapi.org, which serves the USDA map data. Double-check by typing your ZIP code at https://planthardiness.ars.usda.gov/
site.frostSource: NOAA 1991–2020 climate normals (the same period as the 2023 zone map). Nearest stations: Marblehead (USC00194502, ~2 mi) and Beverly (USC00190593, ~5 mi). Retrieved from https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/services/data/v1?dataset=normals-annualseasonal-1991-2020
site.frostConfidenceWhy: These are official NOAA 1991–2020 averages from two stations within about 5 miles, so the typical dates are solid. Any one year can be a week or two off: there's a 1-in-10 chance of frost by Oct 1–5.
site.lastSpringFrostNote: Typical (50/50) last 32°F night: Apr 25 at Marblehead, May 4 at Beverly.
site.safePlantingDateNote: 90% chance the last 32°F night is already past: May 13 at Marblehead, May 17 at Beverly. Use this for dahlias, tomatoes, basil and other tender plants.
site.firstFallFrostNote: Typical (50/50) first 32°F night: Oct 20 at Marblehead, Oct 12 at Beverly.
site.earlyFrostWatchNote: 10% chance of a 32°F night by Oct 1 (Beverly) or Oct 5 (Marblehead). Start watching the forecast from here.
site.hardFreezeNote: Typical first 28°F hard freeze: Oct 25 (Beverly) to Oct 31 (Marblehead). The app uses Oct 25, the earlier of the two.

measured.leftFenceNote: On a slight incline, so the flat distance is a bit shorter.

soil.results: pH about 4.9 (very acidic). Low calcium and magnesium, elevated aluminum, slightly elevated lead. UMass recommended a metals follow-up test before growing food crops.
soil.where: Not mapped yet. The blueberries are on the edge of Zones A and B.
